This petition has been filed by the petitioners under Section 22 of Employee's Compensation Act with regard to death of Mr.Dhanush R. S/o Ramu V in an accident alleged to have been occurred during the course and out of employment of the deceased with respondent No.1.
2.

The case of the claimants in nutshell is that:
The Petitioner Nos.1 & 2 are the father and mother and Petitioner Nos.3 & 4 are the siblings of the deceased - Mr.Dhanush R.
The Deceased was working in the 1 st Respondent Company as Warehouse in charge since 4 years and his Employee Code -153 and was drawing monthly salary of Rs.25,000/-.

Deceased Mr.Dhanush R during his life time, used to attend the duties of 1st respondent every day through bus and returning to his residence after attending the duties and the bus stop was situated very near to 1 st respondent's factory premises.

It is further stated that, on 19.04.2022 Mr.Dhanush R. attended the duties of at 1 st respondent's factory and around 7.00pm after attending of his duties he left the factory to catch the bus at Medanahalli Cross, to reach his home, unfortunately Mr.Dhanush R met with a road traffic accident and he was hit by a motorcycle bearing No.TN-25-AB-9130.

Immediately, he was shifted to Dr.Chandramma Dayananda Sagar Hospital,
Kanakapura SCCH - 25 4 ECA No.73/2023 Road, but unfortunately on the way to the Ramu .V vs Sukhi Print Pack Llp on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95536470/
2 hospital he died due to the injuries sustained by him.

sentences.text: Further, the accident took place in the regular route which the employee was traveling to report to the factory premises and back after completion of his duty hours and the accident was occurred during the course of employment and out of employment.
It is the further case of the petitioners that, the 1 st Respondent having knowledge of accident and death of Mr.Dhanush R and he was an employee under the 1st respondent.
The accident occurred when Mr.Dhanush R was an employee under the respondent No.1 arising out of and during the course of employment.
Hence, this petition.
3. In response to the notice, the respondents have appeared through their respective counsels but not filed written statements.
4. Basing on the pleadings of the parties, the following Points are framed for determination.

1. Whether the petitioners prove that Mr.Dhanush R. mentioned in the petition was the employee under respondent No.1 as Warehouse Incharge on a monthly salary of Rs.25,000/- and there is jural relationship as alleged ?
Whether the petitioners prove the age and wage of Mr. Dhanush R. as alleged ?
3. Whether the petitioners further prove that said Mr.Dhanush R. died in the course of employment as alleged ?

4. Whether the petitioners further prove that they are dependents and legal heirs of deceased Mr.
Dhanush R. as alleged?
5. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation, if so at what rate and at what proportion and at what interest and from whom ?
6. What order or award?
.

The Respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any documents on their behalf.
6. I have heard the arguments canvassed by learned counsel for the petitioners.

8. Point No.4: it is not in dispute that the petitioners are parents and siblings of the deceased.
The petition averments indicates that the petitioners are totally depended on the income of the deceased.

In this regard, I would like to rely on the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in 1 (2021) 11 SCC 780 the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held in paragraph No.8 (a) that:
"If the deceased was a bachelor and claim was filed by the parents, the deduction would normally 50% as personal and living expenses 1 United India Insurance Co.
Ltd Vs Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur and others SCCH - 25 7 ECA No.73/2023 of the bachelor.

sentences.text: Subject to evidence to the contrary, the father was likely to have his own income, and would not considered to be a dependent.
Hence, the mother alone will be considered to be a dependant.

In the absence of any evidence to the contrary, brothers and sisters of the deceased bachelor would not be considered to be a dependents because they would usually either be independent and earning or married, or dependent on the father."
The deceased Mr.Dhanush R. is the elder son and elder brother of the Petitioner Nos.3 and 4.
The petitioners have not placed any documents that the petitioner No.1 is also depended on the income of the deceased.
Though, the petitioners prove that they are legal heirs of the deceased but the petitioner No.1 has failed to prove that he is also dependent on the income of the deceased.
Hence, I answer issue No.4 partly in affirmative.

On the other side, the respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any documents to prove the case.

10. Admittedly the present petition is filed the petitioner under section 22 of Employees Compensation Act claiming the compensation regarding the death of the deceased Mr.Dhanush R.
S/o Ramu V during the course and out of employment of the deceased with respondent No.1.

Hence,
the petitioners ought to have establish there exists jural relationship of employee and employer between the deceased and respondent No.1.

In this connection the petitioners have pleaded in the petition as well as in the evidence that the deceased was employer under the respondent No.1.
11.
The chief examination affidavit of the PW.1 is nothing but a repetition of the petition averments.
The petitioners have produced the reply notice given by the respondent No.1 same is marked as Ex.P12.
On careful reading of the entire document SCCH - 25 9 ECA No.73/2023 the respondent No.1 has not denied the jural relationship.
The petitioners have produced mail correspondence along with reply notice for perusal of the tribunal.
It indicates that, the insurer is not liable to pay the compensation as incident was occurred after completion of the employment.
It is undisputed fact that the employee was attending the duties from his house to company or plant and returned to home from plant through bus.
The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held in the case of MFA No.25462 fo 2011(WC) dated 31.08.20242 in paragraph No.13 and 17 that, "13.

As regarding liability is concerned, the main contention of the insurance company is that there is no connection between the vehicle and death of the deceased and the insurance company is not liable to indemnify the owner.
As discussed above, the lorry was parked by the side of the road and the deceased was taking the bath when he was drowned.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in Malikarjuna G Hiremath as well as Mamtaj bi Bapusab Nadaf dealing with factual 2 The Area Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs Ratnavva and others..

It goes to indicates that the employment of the driver was completed as he was no more the driver of the lorry.

Under such circumstances, it was held that,
the insurance company is not liable."

17. In Mallikarjuna G. Hiremath it was distinguished that, the deceased had completed his journey from Siraguppa to Gurugunta Angreshwar temple, after which he went to the pond and while taking a bath slipped and drowned.
It is identical to the case of Mamtab Bi's Case.
In Poonam Devi's case and in this case facts are identical in nature.

Mamtaj Bi Bapusab Nadaf, Mallikarjuna G. Hiremath,
Kirmani as well as Chandbi's case were decided on the different set of facts.
The employment of the deceased was in force at the time of incident as he was in transit and theory of notional extension came to the aid of the petitioners."
SCCH - 25 11 ECA No.73/2023
The dictum of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka is aptly applicable to the case on hand.

Hence, it can be held that the incident was occurred during substance of the Ramu .V vs Sukhi Print Pack Llp on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95536470/
5 employment or in other words, the employment of the deceased was in force at the time of incident.
It is true that the respondent No.1 has not contested the petition but their reply to the notice caused by the counsel for the petitioners prior to institution of the petition is clearly depicts that the respondent No.1 have clearly admitted the employment of the deceased with them.

sentences.text: As such, it can be hold that, the relationship of employee and employer is established.
12. A perusal of the Aadhar Card indicates that, the deceased was 29 years age at the time of incident.
The documents placed by the petitioners are clearly indicates that, they are legal heirs of the deceased.
The petitioners have contended that the respondent No.1 has paying monthly salary of Rs.25,000/- to deceased per month.
However, the petitioner has not produced any kind of document.
So, the Court has to consider the minimum wages.
As per notification issued by Central Government on 31st May 2010, the monthly wages fixed with effect SCCH - 25 12 ECA No.73/2023 from 31st May 2010 is Rs.8,000/-.

The relevant notification is as under:
"S.O.1258(E) - In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (1B) of Section 4 of the Employee's Compensation Act, 1923, (g of 1923), the Central Government hereby specified, for the purpose of Sub-Section (1) of the said section, the following amount as monthly wages, with effect from the date of publication of this notification in the official gazette, namely - Eight thousand rupees.
"With effect from 3rd January 2020 it is again amended and Rs.15,000/- is fixed."

In the present case on hand, the accident occurred on subsequent to 02.09.2021 and 03.09.2021 So,
looking to the work of the deceased and applying above said notification, the court can take minimum wages at the rate of 15,000/- per month.
13.
Since it is a case of death, the compensation has to be determined as per section 4(1) (a) of the Employees Compensation Act, 1923.
According to section 4(1) (a), where death resulted from the injury, an amount equal to 50% of the SCCH - 25 13 ECA No.73/2023 monthly wages of the deceased multiplied by the relevant factor.
As I observed that deceased was getting Rs.15,000/- per month as salary.
If we take 50% of the said wages, it comes to Rs.7,500/-.
As observed in above paragraph, the deceased has taken as 29 years age at the time of accident.

As per the schedule IV,
the proper factor to the age of 29 years is 209.92.
Therefore, the compensation amount would be 7,500 X 209.92= 15,74,400/-.
In addition to the above mentioned amount, the petitioners are entitled for Rs.20,000/- towards funeral and transportation expenses as per section IV (4) of the Act.

Thus in all the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.15,94,400/-.
14.

The granting of interest in the petition of the present nature is totally governed by section 4A (3)
(a) of the Employees Compensation Act.
According the said provision, the petitioners is entitled for a simple interest thereon at the rate of 12% Per Annum.

As per Rule 60 (b) (ii) of Karnataka Workmen's Compensation Rules, 1966, where the compensation is claimed in the form of a lumpsum under clause (a)(b) or (c) of sub-section (1) of section 4 of the Act, and where the sum claimed exceeds 500/- or fraction thereof, the fees payable is one rupee for each sum of 500/- or fraction thereof.

In view of the above said reasons and discussions, I proceed to pass the following;
 ORDER
The claim petition filed by  SCCH - 25 15 ECA No.73/2023  claimants under Section 22 of  Employee's Compensation Act is  allowed in part with costs.

The petitioner No.2 to 4 are  entitled for the compensation of Rs.15,94,400/- (Rupees Fifteen Lakhs Ninety Four thousand Four Hundred only) with 12% interest per annum from the expiry of one month from the date of accident till the date of deposit of compensation amount by the respondent No.2.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners No.2 to 4 and directed to deposit the compensation amount together with interest within two months from the date of this order.

Out of compensation amount, the petitioner No.2 to 4 are entitled at 60:20:20 ratio and they are entitled to withdraw 75% of their respective SCCH - 25 16 ECA No.73/2023 share and remaining 25% shall be invested as F.D. in any nationalized bank of their choice for a period of three years.

According the said provision, the petitioners is entitled for a simple interest thereon at the rate of 12% Per Annum.

Therefore, in my opinion the respondent No.2/Insurer is liable to indemnify the 1st Respondent/Owner as the policy was in force as on the date of the incident/accident and pay the entire compensation amount of to petitioner No.2 to 4.
16.

As per Rule 60 (b) (ii) of Karnataka Workmen's Compensation Rules, 1966, where the compensation is claimed in the form of a lumpsum under clause (a)(b) or (c) of sub-section (1) of section 4 of the Act, and where the sum claimed exceeds 500/- or fraction thereof, the fees payable is one rupee for each sum of 500/- or fraction thereof.
So the petitioners are liable to pay court fee in accordance with law.

Hence, I answer Point No.1, 2, 5 partly in affirmative and Point No.3 in the affirmatively.
17. Point No.6:

In view of the above said reasons and discussions, I proceed to pass the following;
 ORDER
The claim petition filed by  SCCH - 25 15 ECA No.73/2023  claimants under Section 22 of  Employee's Compensation Act is  allowed in part with costs.

The petitioner No.2 to 4 are  entitled for the compensation of Rs.15,94,400/- (Rupees Fifteen Lakhs Ninety Four thousand Four Hundred only) with 12% interest per annum from the expiry of one month from the date of accident till the date of deposit of compensation amount by the respondent No.2.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners No.2 to 4 and directed to deposit the compensation amount together with interest within two months from the date of this order.

Out of compensation amount, the petitioner No.2 to 4 are entitled at 60:20:20 ratio and they are entitled to withdraw 75% of their respective SCCH - 25 16 ECA No.73/2023 share and remaining 25% shall be invested as F.D. in any nationalized bank of their choice for a period of three years.
